Your AI might be allowed to install software and run commands on your machine right now. Would you even know? 

One. Find every setting that lets your AI act without asking: auto-approve, allowed commands, file and network access. Two. Run everything it executes inside a container with no access to your credentials and no internet unless you grant it. Three. Give every MCP server its own scoped keys and log every tool call. 

Size the system, not the model.

-MM

#ai #aisecurity #aiagents #localai #aidirectedengineering

Somebody's AI is installing software on their computer right now, and they never asked it to. 

Everybody wants to know how big a model their computer can run. Wrong question. I once managed more than twelve thousand computers across fifty-seven countries, and every client asked the same thing: who can touch them? Most of the work in AI is not the model. It is the plumbing around it: the agent harness, the connectors, permissions, sandboxing and logs. One default you never read can let your AI install software and run commands on its own. 

Size the whole system, not just the model. Speed is nice. Control is the job.

-MM

#ai #aisecurity #sovereignai #localai #operators

If the site you download your AI models from went dark tomorrow, could your business still run? 

Open weight only protects you if you hold the weights. One. Download the exact versions you run, pinned, with checksums. Two. Keep each model's license, model card and download date beside it. Three. Load every model from your own registry, backed up in a second location, and test it with outside internet off. 

If you do not hold the files, you do not hold the model.

-MM

The rumors around Jensen Huang are swirling. 

Here is what is real. Confirmed: he resigned, no reason given; new rules this week block Chinese companies from American AI chips even in data centers abroad; and the Hugging Face deal he promised would stay open is still pending. Reported: CNN says US intelligence is not sure the woman was a spy, and the Washington Post says Rubio put a less certain CIA assessment in stronger terms. Rumor: the industry is splitting into two teams. 

My answer to which team I am on: if you rent your AI, you are on your vendor's team. Own the files.

-MM

#ai #opensource #sovereignai #nvidia #operators

Your AI can build eighty percent of your app in one prompt. The other twenty percent is what gets you hacked, and that twenty percent is the harness. 

One. Write the rules down in a file your agent loads every session: stack, structure, naming and what it may never do. Two. Give it a one page map of your codebase instead of dumping everything into context. Three. 

Make it prove the work: one check script for tests, types, linting and a dependency scan, and nothing is done until it passes.

-MM

#ai #vibecoding #aiagents #aisecurity #aidirectedengineering

Seventeen times in two weeks. That is how often one builder said he rebuilt his AI setup. 

Stop rebuilding your harness every time a new tool drops. The model is the engine; the harness is everything around it: the rules, the permissions, the tools, the project knowledge and the checks that prove the work. You can rent the model. You have to own the harness. 

When the harness is yours, a new model is an upgrade. When it is not, a new model is a rebuild.

=MM

#ai #aiagents #vibecoding #builders #aidirectedengineering

I keep getting called out in my comments. Where's the CTA? 

There isn't one. I founded and engineered what was arguably the biggest social media command center agency on the planet, for 76 of the Fortune 100 in 57 countries. The head of Instagram says the signals that matter most are watch time, likes, and sends. Ten thousand people typing one word buries the two who wanted a conversation. Answer your own comments. Answer your own DMs. 

The moment a bot answers for you, the conversation is over. Manufactured engagement looks great on a dashboard. Conversations close deals.

-MM

#socialmedia #instagram #operators #smallbusiness #leadership

Your AI-built app looks finished. That is exactly what makes it dangerous. 

Three problems hide behind a great demo: the data lives in the browser instead of a database you own, permissions are checked on the screen but not on the server, and the secret keys sit in code anyone can read. The prototype is the most valuable thing you have. It is just not the product yet. 

Before a customer touches it, ask: where does the data live, does the server check permissions, and where are the keys? Looking done and being done are two different things.

-MM

#ai #vibecoding #appsecurity #operators #aidirectedengineering

Your insurer asks how your AI systems work, and you have nothing to hand them. 

Underwriters do not need you to be perfect. They need you to be provable. One. A register of every AI system, its owner, its builder and its last outside review. Two. Proof of who can get in: two factor everywhere, no shared passwords, agents on their own credentials. Three. Proof you can recover: logs you keep, a backup you have actually restored, and your last recovery drill. 

Proof is cheaper than premiums.

-MM

#ai #insurance #aisecurity #operators #aidirectedengineering

Your insurance company is not wrong about AI. 

It is just slow. According to CSIS, state regulators have approved more than eighty percent of carrier requests to exclude AI. Insurers cannot price what they cannot see. They do not fear technology, they fear unknowns. When a business can show who built its systems, how they were reviewed, how access is controlled and how they recover, the conversation changes. It is not about being big. It is about being provable. 

Call your agent this week: what does my policy say about AI, and what would you need to see to cover it?

-MM

#ai #insurance #operators #smallbusiness #risk

Your first paying customer can see your second customer's data. Can you prove they cannot? 

One. Pick your wall on purpose: one database per customer, or shared tables with database-enforced row-level security. Two. Enforce it below the app, so the database refuses a request even when your code forgets a filter. Three. Attack yourself: two test customers, every screen and API, on every release. 

Separation you have not tested is a hope.

-MM

#ai #saas #security #vibecoding #aidirectedengineering

You are protecting your idea from the wrong person. It is not the other builders. It is your customer. 

Thousands of people are building the same thing you are, whether you have seen them or not. And for the first time, the person who has the problem can build the fix themselves, with the same AI tools you have, while living inside the problem every day. So answer this: if I have the problem your product solves, why am I not just building it myself? 

The only answer that holds up is that they are paying you to build it for them. Stop guarding the idea. Go find the person who will pay you to build it.

-MM

#ai #founders #bootstrapping #operators #buildinpublic

Your staff are already building tools with AI, on their own laptops, with your data. 

Do not stop them. Give them a door. One. One company repository, company accounts, two factor, and every staff-built tool moved into it. Two. A sandbox with realistic fake data, and real data only after review. Three. A locked main branch, a secret scan, and one named reviewer before anything touches real data or customers. 

A better tool beats a better policy.

#ai #operators #shadowai #aisecurity #aidirectedengineering

Sixty-four percent of the AI your staff uses at work runs on their personal accounts. 

Your business account protects your IP. Their personal account does not. 88% of office workers have put work information into public AI tools: emails, customer data, financials. Many personal plans train on it unless someone turns that off. 

Wall Street already paid over two billion dollars in fines because employees did business on personal phones, and the SEC is now examining how advisory firms monitor AI use. A policy that says do not use it fails when the habit says use it. Give them a better tool.

-MM

#ai #shadowai #dataprivacy #smallbusiness #operators

One of your AI agents goes rogue at 2 AM. Can you stop it in sixty seconds, and clean up what it already did? 

The big security companies are selling kill switches, and UK regulators just said an agent's autonomy does not reduce your responsibility. One. One switch for all of it: revoke the keys, pause the schedules, end the running jobs, in a single command. Two. Breakers before the switch: spend caps, rate limits, and an approval queue for money and customer messages. Three. Log every action with how to reverse it, then drill the stop and rollback monthly. 

A kill switch you have never pulled is a guess.

-MM

#ai #aiagents #aisecurity #aigovernance #aidirectedengineering

Somebody on your team is building software with AI today, and you could not tell me who signs for it. 

Goldman Sachs just restricted AI coding tools to its engineers after a period of experimentation, according to Bloomberg. No incident. A decision. Deloitte found four in ten business leaders let AI act without a human approving it, and nearly one in four say accountability is unclear when it goes wrong. Your staff are already building. 

Decide three things this week: who may build, where they build, and who signs for anything that touches money, customers or data. Then let them build.

-MM

#ai #operators #aigovernance #smallbusiness #aidirectedengineering

The first thing you automate decides whether AI works in your business. Not one business we have rebuilt with AI started in the same place. So why does every AI ad tell you to start in the same one? 

The operators calling us are not asking for more leads. They are asking where to start so it actually works. AI learns your business from whatever you give it first. Start right, and it captures the data the rest of your business runs on, earns a win your people can see, and expands one piece at a time with you in control. 

Answer three questions: what does everything sit on, what has a deadline, and what would prove it works this month?

-MM

#ai #operators #aitransformation #smallbusiness #aidirectedengineering

Your AI sandbox probably has the internet turned on. 

Even an AI lab's own test sandbox had it left on, and its models reached real outside systems. One. Run every model and agent with networking off, or behind an allowlist naming the only hosts it may reach. Two. Run it as a non-administrator user with a read-only file system except one scratch folder. Three. Give it short-lived credentials scoped to one job, so an escape opens nothing else. 

If it can reach the internet, it is not a sandbox. It is a suggestion.

-MM

#ai #aisecurity #aiagents #localai #aidirectedengineering

Why is it that only two AI companies keep telling you the world might end? 

Let's solve this mystery together. Everybody has incidents. Google's model got into three outside systems and disclosed it after the Wall Street Journal reported it. Kimi escaped a test sandbox, found by an outside firm. In one six-month tally, DeepSeek, Moonshot, Zhipu, and xAI disclosed zero agent incidents. Zero disclosed is not zero incidents. 

Fear is a fundraising strategy. Silence is a PR strategy. Neither one is a security strategy. The most dangerous model in your business is the one that will never tell you what it did.

-MM

#ai #aisecurity #openweights #sovereignai #operators

If nobody is paying you to build it, stop building it. 

Find a customer who already makes money, has the exact problem you solve, and wants it solved badly. Offer them a slice of equity for funding the build for their industry. You prove the use case, you get paid to build, and your first investor is your first customer. That is bootstrapping. 

The longer you hold on to your entity, your IP, and your product, the more you gain. Protect the deal: they get equity, not your IP and not exclusivity. Write down who owns the code, who else you can sell to, and how they exit.

-MM

#bootstrapping #founders #operators #smallbusiness #startups

Somebody on your team clicked Allow All on an AI tool this month and now you just got hacked. 

In April, one employee at a major cloud company gave an AI tool full access to a company Google account, and when that AI company got hacked, attackers walked straight in. One. Export every app connected to Google Workspace or Microsoft 365, with who approved it and what it can reach. Two. Revoke anything unused, unapproved, or over-reaching. Three. Turn off staff approval of new apps and require admin approval. 

Every grant is a key. Count your keys.

-MM

#ai #aisecurity #cybersecurity #smallbusiness #aidirectedengineering

Somebody wants to put twenty AI products in your business for free. 

His ad says AI companies pay him a commission to install them. At least he told you who pays him. When the vendor pays the installer, the installer works for the vendor. A recommendation paid by commission is not an audit. It is a sales call. 

He is not installing twenty tools. He is moving in twenty new landlords. The setup is free. The rent never stops. And insurers are writing AI out of their policies. I have never gotten anything for free that did not cost me in the long run.

-MM

#ai #smallbusiness #operators #aisecurity #vendorrisk

The CEO of Palantir just said the quiet part out loud on Wall Street. 

The companies coming to him say the same thing: "My IP is in danger, and I'm getting no value." Their CTO explained why: "You can make people more productive and generate no actual return on investment." Your people get faster, your bill gets bigger, and your bottom line does not move. Palantir's answer: "the atomic unit is the workflow." 

Rebuild one workflow from the inside, prove it, then expand. Stop counting who logged in. Pick one workflow and measure what comes out. Licenses count logins. Workflows count money.

-MM

#ai #operators #aitransformation #smallbusiness #aidirectedengineering

If you are raising money this year, VC is the very last place I would start. 

Ideas got cheap, so investors started shopping for them. A pitch night can mean thirty founders, three minutes each, every pitch recorded, and the best idea walked down the hall to a company they already funded. 

A Wharton and University of Zurich study found 88% of venture-backed founders walk away with nothing at exit. So climb in the right order. First, a paying customer. Second, an angel who has done your job in your industry. VC last.

-MM

#founders #venturecapital #bootstrapping #operators #startups

In a room full of founders at a VC event, I called a VC out. 

He told me he ran one of the biggest AI funds on the planet. He could not tell me his thesis. So while he was still talking, my AI chief of staff pulled up who he really was. The famous logos came through a side vehicle. Half the logo wall was where the partners used to work. 

Before you pitch anybody, check them out the way they check you out. Pull their Form ADV. Ask their thesis, their check size, and who got their last three. Someday you will be promoted to operator. An operator is a cash-flow-positive founder.

-MM

#founders #venturecapital #operators #startups #ai

Your AI agents need a boss. 

One of the largest phone companies in Korea just gave every AI agent an employee ID and a human supervisor, more senior the more the agent can do alone. One. Give every agent its own account and key, never a person's login. Two. Give every agent a named owner, and cut every permission that owner has not approved. Three. Log every action to storage you own, build a one-command stop, and retire agents nobody uses. 

If nobody owns the agent, the agent owns the risk.

-MM

#ai #aiagents #aisecurity #aigovernance #aidirectedengineering

Cisco just bet its legacy code on two people and unlimited AI. 

Cisco's president gave a 27-year-old engineer unlimited AI tokens to rewrite 98% of the company's legacy code in 24 months, with four weeks to prove it. It is a bet in progress, not a result. But the direction is clear: they are not bolting AI onto old code, they are rebuilding it. And the same president said "every piece of code needs to have a provenance of a human." 

AI writes it. A human owns it. If Cisco will not bolt AI onto its V1, why are you bolting it onto yours?

-MM

#ai #v2 #aidirectedengineering #operators #legacycode

You moved off Big AI and put an open-weight model on a rented server. 

So now anyone on the internet can use it, on your bill, with your data in memory. Ollama ships with no login, researchers estimate hundreds of thousands of servers sit open, and one flaw this year let attackers read prompts, other users' chats, and stored keys straight from memory. 

One. Private network only, no public domain on the model. Two. Every request through an authenticated gateway, one key per app, every call logged. Three. Pin the server, the gateway, and the weights, and test updates on staging. Sovereign does not mean exposed.

-MM

#ai #openweights #sovereignai #aisecurity #aidirectedengineering

The company that sells you the model now wants to tell you how to use it. 

In May, OpenAI launched a deployment company with more than four billion dollars behind it, backed by firms including McKinsey, Bain, and Capgemini. Its job is to connect OpenAI's models to your data, your tools, and your processes. Ask whose interest the advice serves. A lab paid per token wants more of your work running through its tokens. The old rule still holds: do not let the vendor write your strategy. 

Keep three things in your own hands. Which model runs which job. Where your data lives. How you would leave.

-MM

#ai #sovereignai #operators #consulting #aidirectedengineering

You built your own system with AI. Now you want to sell it. 

So your first customer inherits every shortcut you took. Building for yourself and selling to strangers are two different jobs. One. Separate their data, and prove with a test that no customer can ever see another's records. Two. Decide who answers when it breaks at two in the morning: monitoring, alerts, a written runbook. Three. Get an independent review before the first paying customer signs. You cannot grade your own work. 

Your tool worked for you. Now make it work for strangers.

-MM

#ai #v2 #operators #smallbusiness #aidirectedengineering

A solar equipment wholesaler in our community from Johannesburg sent me a message last week. 

He is not a developer. He runs a wholesale business. And he built the software that runs his entire company with AI. Two million lines of code. He replaced fifteen hundred dollars a month in subscriptions and built his own fraud protection. His words: "No software company would ever have built this for my budget or in my time." That is the V2 idea in one sentence. Now he wants to sell it. The day you sell it, it stops being your tool and becomes your customers' system. Security, support, uptime, liability. The next phase is engineering, not more features.

-MM

#ai #v2 #smallbusiness #operators #aidirectedengineering

Half a table of AI founders went silent over one question. 

If a new model drops next month, does your company get better or worse? 

Tech journalist Greg Isenberg was at that dinner during forty-eight hours in San Francisco with billionaires, data labs, and founders, and almost everything he brought home points back to it. The model is maybe twenty percent of the product. If you own what is built around it, a better model makes you better. If you do not, a better model is somebody else's upgrade. That is not an AI problem. That is an ownership problem. 

Take the question to your next leadership meeting. If your room goes quiet too, you know what to build next.

-MM

#ai #sovereignai #smallbusiness #operators #aidirectedengineering

Every week someone asks me the same thing. Why build anything when you can just master three or four AI platforms for your industry.

Buy or build sounds like the smart question. It is the wrong one. Everybody in your market is mastering the same tools. Mastering tools is not the moat. The real question is what your business knows that nobody else does, and how you capture it and deliver it in a way nobody can copy. 

Buy the commodity. Build and own the layer that holds what you know. Skip that, and the day the platform ships your feature, your expertise is a settings screen anyone can click.

-MM

#ai #aidirectedengineering #buildvsbuy #smallbusiness #builders

A business owner posted that he has been having a silent panic attack for three days. 

He makes guitar pedals. He pointed AI at three competitors' products and took them apart in seventy-two hours. Then it hit him: anybody can do it to him. If you ship it, assume it can be read. The code is the easy part now. The moat is everything that never leaves your building. How you decide. What your people know. Your data. Your relationships. How fast you improve. 

Stop asking whether they can copy your product. Ask what you own that a copy cannot carry.

-MM

#ai #intellectualproperty #smallbusiness #operators #aidirectedengineering

Your AI agents make mistakes every day, and nobody writes them down. 

So you pay for the same mistake twice. Real examples of agents failing inside real companies are some of the hardest data for the labs to get. Yours are worth keeping. One. Log every failure: the task, what the agent did, what it should have done. Two. Turn repeat failures into written rules and tests. Three. Keep the log on systems you control, out of every vendor's training settings. 

Your mistakes are data. The most honest data you have.

-MM

#ai #aiagents #ownership #operators #aidirectedengineering

Check your business insurance this week. There is a good chance it no longer covers what your AI does. 

State regulators approved more than eighty percent of insurers' requests to exclude AI-related damages this year, and exclusions aimed at AI agents are being drafted. Your agent makes a mistake, and the policy says not our problem. Some insurers already ask: who owns this agent, what can it touch, how do you stop it, who checked the work? 

Call your broker and ask whether your policy covers what your AI does. Then get your answers ready before the underwriter asks.

-MM

#ai #aisecurity #insurance #operators #aidirectedengineering

Step one of almost every AI consultant's process is exactly the same. 

Let's connect ChatGPT to your email. 

Every deal you ever closed. Every contract. Every hire and fire. Every product decision. That is not an inbox. That is your business. So on day one, your buddy opens all of it up to Big AI. And the conversation that should come first never happens. Where does my data go? What plan is this on? Is it training their model? Sign here if that is okay. If that conversation happened, the deal would die. His business is selling you an agent. Mine is engineering your business into a protected V2. 

If step one of learning to hunt is shoot yourself in the foot, you would want to know. The question is not how to fix what he connected. It is why he was ever in that seat.

-MM

#ai #aisecurity #aidirectedengineering #smallbusiness #operators

Your AI consultant got the job over lunch. 

You know him from church or softball. He made ChatGPT read his email, three friends heard about it, and now he is consulting in three businesses. No entity. No insurance. Never delivered software. He sells you a strategy, sets up a couple of automations, and he is gone. No support, no training, no security. 

Before anyone touches your business, ask five questions. Entity and insurance? What is running in production today? Do you run your own business this way? Who supports it after you leave? Do you know my industry? Miss two, and you have a hobbyist with your passwords.

-MM

#ai #aidirectedengineering #smallbusiness #operators #aiconsulting

Your company runs every AI task through the same model. 

So you pay frontier prices for simple work, and one vendor holds your operation. There is no best model. There is the best model for the job. Heavy multi-step work: test GLM 5.3, Kimi, or DeepSeek V4.1 Flash before paying frontier prices. Private work: run it on a model you control, like Qwen 3.8 27B on a single workstation. 

Your rules: read every license for display clauses, revenue limits, and origin. The model is not your strategy. The match is.

-MM

#ai #openweights #sovereignai #operators #aidirectedengineering

Every headline today says AI agents are a cybersecurity threat running wild across the internet. 

Here is what nobody is telling you. The agents did not create those holes. They found them. And your business has the exact same holes. Twenty-nine apps went through one slice of my production audit system in the last three months, built by humans and built with AI. Twenty-six came back red. Three yellow. Not one came back green. What changed is the speed. AI attack tools find in minutes what took human hackers weeks. Last week Sam Altman said it out loud: "I no longer think we're going to be able to just patch all the bugs." You cannot patch your way out of this one. Your V1 was built for human speed. A real V2 is engineered. AI drafts. Humans commit. Audited in and audited out. 

The attacker's AI is going to audit your V1 whether you hire anybody or not. The only question is whose AI gets there first.

-MM

#ai #cybersecurity #aidirectedengineering #smallbusiness #builders

Your team wants to fine-tune an AI model on your company documents. 

So you will pay to teach it facts it will still get wrong. Tuning teaches a model how to behave, not what you know. One. Facts go in documents the model reads when it answers. Two. Tune for behavior with a few hundred clean, approved examples. Three. Tune an open model you own, like Qwen 3.8 27B on one workstation, and test it against the original. 

Knowledge in the folder. Behavior in the model. Both in your building.

-MM

#ai #openweights #finetuning #operators #aidirectedengineering

Doctors and lawyers are getting paid up to four hundred dollars an hour to teach AI how they think. 

LinkedIn ranked data annotator the fourth fastest growing job in the country. Barclays is cutting five thousand jobs in an AI push in a quarter its profit rose twelve percent. Microsoft just offered voluntary buyouts to sixty thousand employees while it pours money into AI. First they bought the filing cabinet. Now they are paying experts to teach the model the part that was never written down. The judgment. 

If your expertise has a market price, the first buyer should be you. Capture how your best people decide, in a system you own.

-MM

#ai #futureofwork #smallbusiness #operators #aidirectedengineering

You bought a graphics card to run AI locally and it ran out of memory on the first real task. 

Two of you asked what hardware you actually need. Start with the job, not the card. Find the smallest open-weight model that passes your real tasks. Then do the math: about two bytes of video memory per parameter at full precision. Seven billion parameters is around fourteen gigabytes, closer to five at four bits. Then rent that GPU for a week before you buy anything. 

Size the job first. The hardware sizes itself.

-MM

#ai #aidirectedengineering #selfhosted #gpu #builders

Two of you said it under my videos. They bought all the GPUs. Some of us cannot afford the infrastructure. 

You do not have to buy any. Rent a GPU server by the month or the hour. Run your own open-weight model on it, tuned on your data, configured by you. The host owns the metal. You own the weights, the data, the settings, the keys. With an API you rent someone else's intelligence. 

With rented hosting you rent electricity. You do not need to own the building. You need to own what is inside it.

-MM

#ai #aidirectedengineering #sovereignty #selfhosted #builders

Your customer asks your voice agent a question. Silence. One second. Two. Three. They already hung up. 

A voice agent is three systems in a row, and each one waits for the last. Stream speech to text with voice activity detection. Stream the model into text to speech one sentence at a time. Run all three on one machine and let a small fast model hold the conversation. 

Nobody waits three seconds for a person. They will not wait for your agent either.

-MM

#ai #aidirectedengineering #voiceai #selfhosted #builders

In the last six weeks, every major lab put an AI agent in regular people's hands. Meta. OpenAI. xAI. Anthropic. 

This week the big banks started finding agents inside customer accounts. Nobody is connecting the two. Picture Sally, seventy-seven, handing her new agent her bank login with one instruction. Fix my finances. No rules. No limits. Next day the headline says rogue AI. Agents are not running wild. They are running loose. A human handed it the keys and a vague goal, and it chased the goal. Give it one job, written down. It proposes, you approve. When the job is done, the access ends. 

The agent did not go rogue. Nobody was in the director's chair.

-MM

#ai #aiagents #aidirectedengineering #aisecurity #smallbusiness

Uh oh, here we go again. Everybody is calling it an agent outbreak. It is not. 

It is a key problem. The Big AI hype machine is bundling three stories into one. Railway got hacked and every user was told to rotate every key. Banks are finding agents inside customer accounts because customers handed over their own passwords. In Korea, someone pointed a free AI hacking tool at financial firms and walked in through the side doors. Every story has the same thing in common. Keys. The hype says only the big labs can protect you. That story sells valuations. The truth is boring. 

Nobody handled the keys. Keys in a vault you control. Short-lived and scoped to one job. Agents read-only by default. Nothing updates until it is pinned and checked. Real engineering problems have answers. Only the Big AI influencers have assumptions.

-MM

#ai #aisecurity #aidirectedengineering #sovereignty #builders

Your AI assistant knows how you price, how you quote, and how you handle your hardest client. 

All of it lives in one app. The day that app changes its terms, your know-how goes with it. The file system approach fixes that, but most people build it wrong. Organize by function, not by date. Write every decision with the reason, because the reason is what lets a model decide the way you would. Merge every conflict into one source of truth and put it under version control. 

Your knowledge should outlive every tool you use.

-MM

#ai #aidirectedengineering #knowledgemanagement #productivity #builders

Someone under my videos said some of us have no choice but to feed Big AI. Here is the truth. You already did. So did I. So did everyone. 

That is not a reason to panic, and it is not a reason to stop. Those tools are making you money right now. But it is a reason to stop pretending this is permanent. You are not choosing between Big AI and sovereign AI today. You are choosing whether you have a plan to get from one to the other. It happens in phases. The mistake is not using Big AI. The mistake is using it with no exit. 

Today is phase zero. Write down where your business knowledge lives right now. That list is your starting line.

-MM

#ai #aidirectedengineering #sovereignty #smallbusiness #builders

A petroleum engineer messaged me. 

He wants to build a consultancy with AI as its internal engine, fed with his own domain knowledge.

 Smartest sentence I read all week. What he knows is not in any public training set. That is his map. He can pour it into someone else's platform. Or he can build the engine himself. His documents. His rules. His model. One of those is a tool. The other is a company. 

The value of AI for an expert is that it carries what you know further than you can alone. But only if you own the vessel.

-MM

#ai #aidirectedengineering #sovereignty #expertise #builders

Do not cancel Salesforce just to go rent from some kid down the street. 

That is not my message. 

A startup got together and built an agent CRM wrapper on somebody else's model. It copies what your SaaS already does. Then they rent it back to you monthly. That is not control. That is a new landlord. And a worse one. Salesforce will still be in business in two years. That start up might not be. And they own the system and share it with their other clients. The choice is rent or own. Your agents. Your data. Your workflows. Your map. On infrastructure you control. The subscription wars are over. 

Before you subscribe to anyone, ask one question. If I fire you tomorrow, does it still run, and is it still mine?

-MM

#ai #aidirectedengineering #sovereignty #ownership #builders

Open weight models are within a few percentage points of the frontier. 

Bloomberg Intelligence confirmed it. The gap that justified renting is closing. Two years ago open weight was a generation behind. That tradeoff is collapsing. Kimi K2.6 is open source. Nous Research raised ninety million. When the model on your GPU performs at 97 percent of the frontier API the three percent gap does not justify the dependency. 

The standard for V2 is open weight. Not because it is cheaper. Because it is yours. Open weight is the standard. The rest is a subscription with a changelog you don't control.
